compliance_deadlines: By 2026: formulate more than 50 new national and industry AI standards, promote and implement standards across more than 1,000 enterprises, and participate in formulating more than 20 international standards (non-binding policy targets)
policy_extraction.implementation_notes: The 2024 edition of the National AI Industry Comprehensive Standardization System Construction Guide serves as a non-binding national standardization roadmap and technical taxonomy rather than a directly enforceable regulation. It organizes China's AI standard system into seven pillars—foundational common standards, foundational support (data, chips, compute), key technologies (including large models, agents, embodied AI, and biometrics), smart products and services, enabling new industrialization, industry applications, and safety/governance (including security testing, content labeling, ethical risk assessment, and ethics review). Implementation relies on standardization technical organizations, industry associations, talent development, and voluntary enterprise benchmarking, with no mandatory legal duties or sanctions specified. Specific issuing ministries are not printed inside the attachment text.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document's dominant rationale is economic competitiveness: its preamble, industry status analysis, and overarching goals frame AI standardization primarily as a strategic lever to cultivate 'new quality productive forces,' upgrade manufacturing, build China into a manufacturing and digital powerhouse, seize first-mover advantage in the AI industry, and expand global industrial influence. Innovation enablement is a strong secondary frame, as the guide emphasizes innovation-driven linkages between R&D and standards, enterprise adoption, and scenario-based deployment across sectors; however, economic competitiveness edges it out because technological innovation and standard adoption are explicitly subordinated to national industrial upgrading and global market positioning. Consumer and public safety appears as a modest secondary frame through full-lifecycle product, system, and operational safety standards intended to underpin secure industrial development, while fairness and explainability appear only briefly under ethical governance standards.
